Title: Macron arrives in Malaysia for two-day official visit
Article:
SEPANG: French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Malaysia today to begin a two-day official visit aimed at further strengthening bilateral relations between the two countries.
The aircraft carrying Macron, his wife Brigitte Macron and their delegation landed at the Bunga Raya Complex of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) at 11.10 pm, where he was received by Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo.
Macron later inspected a guard of honour comprising 28 officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment.
The arrival ceremony was also enlivened by a cultural performance featuring traditional dances and rhythmic percussion, showcasing Malaysia's rich and diverse cultural heritage.
The visit, at the invitation of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, is Macron's first to Malaysia since he assumed office in May 2017.
Tomorrow, the French president will be accorded an official welcoming ceremony at the Sultan Abdul Samad Building in Kuala Lumpur, followed by a bilateral meeting with Anwar.
The meeting is expected to focus on elevating Malaysia-France relations to a Strategic Partnership, reflecting the growing depth and strategic significance of the longstanding ties between the two countries.
The two leaders are also scheduled to witness the exchange of several memoranda of understanding (MoUs) covering key areas of cooperation, including defence, higher education, critical minerals and energy transition.
Anwar will subsequently host an official luncheon in honour of the French president.
In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and France amounted to RM17.78 billion (US$4.17 billion).
Malaysia's exports to France were valued at RM6.05 billion (US$1.41 billion), with electrical and electronic products constituting the principal export category.
Imports from France totalled RM11.73 billion (US$2.76 billion), comprising mainly transport equipment, machinery and chemicals.
France is Malaysia's 21st-largest trading partner globally and its fourth-largest trading partner among European countries. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar demands bold UN overhaul, urges abolition of Security Council veto
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the United Nations (UN) to undertake bolder reforms, including abolishing the veto power, which has long prevented the world body's Security Council from acting fairly and effectively.
Emphasising this at the 16th Asean-UN Summit in Manila, the Philippines, Anwar said the current structure of the UN Security Council required a comprehensive overhaul to ensure the UN remained relevant and capable of addressing humanitarian crises and global conflicts without being constrained by the interests of major powers.
Anwar said he had also outlined the need to translate the Asean-UN Plan of Action 2026-2030 into tangible outcomes, particularly in green and digital transitions, climate resilience and sustainable development.
"Asean must also continue to uphold the principle of Asean Centrality and the supremacy of international law in navigating increasingly challenging geopolitical competition," he said in a Facebook post.
On the situation in the Middle East, Anwar stressed that Malaysia strongly condemned the continued atrocities of forced displacement and starvation inflicted on the Palestinian people.
"We demand an immediate and lasting ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian aid delivery, protection for humanitarian workers and full membership for Palestine in the UN," he said.
Meanwhile, in his address at the Asean-Australia Summit, the prime minister stressed the need to strengthen the multilateral system, respect international law and enhance cooperation in addressing cybersecurity threats and artificial intelligence (AI) risks.
He said the Asean-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, which entered its fifth year, served as an important platform to elevate relations further through more concrete, balanced and mutually beneficial cooperation.
"Malaysia sees ample scope to expand cooperation in trade and investment, energy security, climate transition and digital transformation," he said.
He said efforts to develop more resilient regional supply and value chains, particularly in critical minerals, should also be prioritised through technology transfer, investment and expertise development to ensure prosperity was shared more equitably.
"Malaysia also expressed concern over escalating conflicts in (the Middle East), including attacks on Saudi Arabia, and called for intensified diplomatic efforts to ease tensions and address the root causes of the conflicts," he said.
Anwar is leading the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, which are being held from Nov 15 to 17 under the Philippines' chairmanship, themed Navigating Our Future, Together.

Title: Malaysia, China agree to deepen AI cooperation, technology transfer
Article:
MANILA: China has agreed to strengthen cooperation with Malaysia and other Asean member states, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI) technology transfer, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Describing the agreement as a positive development, Anwar said AI cooperation was among the key areas discussed with dialogue partners during the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits here.
He said the discussions also covered cybersecurity.
"In all our discussions with Asean countries, Australia and South Korea, we emphasised the importance of intensifying efforts in artificial intelligence.
"However, in our specific discussions with China, we agreed to enhance cooperation in AI, including technology transfer and additional training for Malaysia and other Asean member states," he said.
Anwar also stressed the importance of ensuring that micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) benefit from regional economic cooperation, particularly in AI, energy and trade.
He said Asean's economic agenda must be inclusive and should not focus solely on large-scale investments.
Anwar said MSMEs remained a key pillar of the economies of Asean member states and must not be left behind as the region strengthens economic cooperation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar warns delay in South China Sea CoC talks could invite outside interference
Article:
MANILA: Delays in finalising the Code of Conduct (CoC) negotiations on the South China Sea could create an opening for external powers to intervene, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
However, he said Asean and China had yet to set a new deadline for concluding negotiations on the code.
Anwar said Malaysia wanted the issue resolved through direct negotiations between Asean and China, in line with Asean centrality, rather than allowing the region to become an arena for major-power rivalry.
"It is critical because we have seen this matter delayed for so long. Initially, we set a timeline until the end of the year, but I also acknowledge that there has been progress and a much more positive commitment from China.
"I strongly urge that this matter not be delayed further. I do not want other powers to intervene and use this vacuum to claim a role for themselves," he said.
He did not rule out the negotiations extending beyond the original year-end target, citing progress acknowledged by Asean leaders and Chinese Premier Li Qiang during the Asean-China Summit.
"When there is clear progress in the negotiations, we should not impose a deadline that could undermine the process.
"If there is no progress, I can understand the need to set a deadline. However, in this case, negotiations are moving positively," he told the media on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit here.
Anwar said Malaysia also emphasised the importance of ensuring freedom of navigation and the safety of all forms of transport and travel, including maritime and air routes, in the South China Sea.

Title: Esscom officer alleges police assaulted wife, brought children to station during murder probe
Article:
TAWAU: An Esscom officer has claimed that he faced pressure during investigations into the murder of e-hailing driver Nurman Bakaratu, including allegations that his wife was assaulted and their three children brought to the Tawau district police headquarters to force him to accept the investigators' version of events.
Inspector John Kennedy Anak Sanggah, 47, the 13th plaintiff witness, said in his witness statement that the incident involving his children took place on Feb 6, 2023, while he and his wife, Vivien Fabian, were in remand.
Their children were then aged 6, 3 and 9 months.
He alleged that the move was intended to exert emotional pressure on them to comply with the investigating team's demands.
However, during cross-examination by Senior Federal Counsel Mardziatun Nisa Ahamadul Kaber, John disagreed with the suggestion that the children had been brought to the police headquarters for their welfare and to allow them to meet their parents.
He also rejected the suggestion that his allegation of the police using the children as a threat was an emotional embellishment intended to discredit the investigation.
John further alleged that his wife had been slapped, beaten and forced to remove her clothes during questioning while in custody.
However, he admitted that he was not present in the women's interrogation room and that much of what he knew about the alleged treatment came from his wife.
He also agreed that lock-up records did not mention facial swelling, identify the alleged assailant or record the claim that she had been forced to undress. No photographs of the alleged injuries or official medical report were produced in court.
During re-examination by plaintiff's counsel Kamaruddin Mohmad Chinki, John said he had personally seen his wife's swollen cheek and bruises on her back after the incident.
He also referred to a lock-up movement record dated Feb 4, 2023, at 3.11pm, which recorded her complaint of body aches and redness and bruising on the back of one shoulder.
John maintained that he was not involved in Nurman's murder and was in Lahad Datu with his wife on Jan 13, 2023, when the victim was killed.

Title: Trial opening of US man accused of killing British woman he met on fetish website
Article:
MIAMI: A Florida man goes on trial on Monday for the murder of a British woman who allegedly traveled to the United States to be killed.
Dwain Hall, 54, is accused of kidnapping and murdering Sonia Exelby in October 2025 after the two had corresponded over the internet.
According to prosecutors, Hall and the 32-year-old Exelby had communicated for about two years using a fetish website called "Motherless.com" and an encrypted application called Sessions.
The now-defunct Motherless features "content that depicted various fetishes, including extreme BDSM, torture, and rape material," according to court documents.
During their exchanges, Exelby, who reportedly struggled with mental health issues, allegedly expressed a desire to be murdered.
She traveled to Gainesville, Florida, on October 10, 2025, and was picked up at the airport by Hall, according to prosecutors.
Hall, who went by the username "AlphaSadist" on Motherless.com is accused of sexually abusing Exelby during the course of the next week and stabbing her to death.
Her body was found buried in a shallow grave near Hall's residence.
Hall was arrested after attempting to use Exelby's credit card.
Prosecutors plan to use messages exchanged between the pair, along with images recovered from Hall's phone, to prove their case.
Florida currently executes more convicted murderers than any other US state but prosecutors will not seek the death penalty in Hall's case.
According to The Telegraph, British authorities agreed to share evidence with US prosecutors only on condition that the death penalty would not be pursued. — AFP

Title: Asean must strengthen military readiness before crises erupt, says Khaled
Article:
MELAKA: Asean member states must strengthen collective military readiness before crises emerge, amid an increasingly complex and unpredictable regional security landscape.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said no country could consider itself immune to threats beyond its borders, particularly amid growing cyber threats, technological advances and other non-traditional security challenges.
He said defence cooperation must be strengthened through mutual understanding, effective communication and joint response mechanisms to ensure armed forces could act swiftly during emergencies.
"Collective readiness cannot be built when a crisis is already unfolding. Instead, it must be developed well before a crisis erupts," he said.
He was speaking at a dinner in conjunction with the 27th Asean Chiefs of Army Multilateral Meeting (ACAMM) and the 14th Asean Sergeants Major Annual Meeting (ASWAM) 2026 in Banda Hilir here last night.
Also present were Army chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman, Asean army chiefs and senior military officers.
Khaled said collective readiness did not mean adopting a uniform military approach or compromising national sovereignty, but ensuring cooperation mechanisms were in place when needed.
He also stressed that Asean must uphold unity, neutrality and non-alignment to preserve Southeast Asia as a Zone of Peace, Freedom and Neutrality (ZOPFAN).

Title: Europe's trade walls cannot keep China out as investments soar
Article:
CHINA  doesn't need to clear Europe's trade barriers. It can build inside them.
Chinese firms are establishing production and supplier networks across Central and Eastern Europe, which could enable them to gain more control over the technologies and inputs that European manufacturing needs.
China is increasingly challenging the European Union in the advanced manufacturing sectors that helped the EU weather the first China shock, which reshaped global manufacturing in the 2000s.
Chinese firms are competing with the EU in chemicals, machinery, advanced equipment and autos — and increasingly coming out on top on price and quality.
The EU trade deficit with China has nearly quadrupled over the past decade, from around 100 billion euros in 2014 to over 370 billion euros last year, or roughly one billion euros a day, according to Eurostat data.
France and Germany are seeking to push back with stronger trade defences, but import curbs will achieve little if Chinese investment, ownership and control of critical technologies recreates the same vulnerabilities inside the single market.
Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) appear to be key to China's growth strategy in Europe.
For example, Slovenia's goods deficit with China rose from 2.5 per cent to 16 per cent over that period. Investment and corporate ties deepened that exposure.
Last year, Chinese foreign direct investment (FDI) flows into the EU approached 16.8 billion euros, and the cumulative value of Chinese investment in the bloc was about 95 billion euros, according to Eurostat and Rhodium Group data.
While most legacy Chinese FDI in Europe centred on Germany, France and the Benelux countries, the focus has shifted east in recent years.
CEE has attracted more than half of Chinese FDI into the EU and Britain since 2021, according to an analysis by the Rhodium Group, with an even larger regional share when the Western Balkans are included.
Hungary has attracted the largest share of new investment since the Covid-19 pandemic, hitting 44 per cent in 2023 and 23 per cent last year.
The investment surge in CEE has largely been driven by mega-projects in the electric vehicle (EV) supply chain. Chinese EV and battery manufacturers CATL, BYD and Sunwoda are all establishing major Hungarian operations.
Slovakia has attracted investment from Chinese battery tech firm Gotion and will be the site of a new plant owned by Volvo Cars, the carmaker majority-owned by China's Geely Holding.
Meanwhile, Serbia, which has significant steel and copper assets, has signed contracts with Chinese auto firms Minth, Shanghai Automotive Chassis, BMTS Technology and Xingyu Automotive, envisaging around one billion euros in investment and nearly 1,700 car-parts jobs.
The deals also include a new robotics factory in Sabac, billed as Europe's first humanoid robot mass production base.
These investments can create jobs, spur growth, and accelerate the energy transition, but they may also erode EU competitiveness over time.
Outsourcing key advanced manufacturing technologies to Chinese entities risks deepening Europe's dependence on external supply chains and weakening domestic innovation and research and development.
Europe is seeking to limit China's access to its consumer markets and industries, but the current Franco-German push for faster defensive trade action and tougher investment screening across the bloc appears to be too little too late.
Europe's flagship proposal, the Industrial Accelerator Act, leaves manufacturers' key competitiveness gaps unaddressed.
Moreover, its screening mechanism would largely leave unexamined Chinese control via ultimate ownership, foreign subsidies and supply-chain concentration — some key issues when looking at CEE's growing dependence.
There is also the problem of fragmentation across the bloc. Investment deals might be in one country's interest but could weaken the bloc's collective negotiating position with Beijing.
To address this, the continent would likely need a permanent European economic security coordination mechanism to unite trade, competition and national screening authorities that could identify risks before investments become irreversible.
Yet the chances of forming such a body at a time of growing political fragmentation within EU countries seem slim.
And, ultimately, protectionism cannot compensate for the region's structural problems, including expensive energy, fragmented capital markets and slow industrial innovation.
For that, the region would likely need to create a true energy union and invest in technological innovation.
Building trade walls buys time, but not true change.
The writer is director of the Geoeconomics Program of the Center for the Study of Democracy

Title: Bukit Aman probing Malaysian drug syndicate after Thailand seizes 240kg of meth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman is working with Thai authorities to identify a suspected Malaysian drug syndicate following the arrest of five Malaysians and seizure of 240kg of methamphetamine in Thailand last week.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the department, through its Kedah and Perlis teams, was seeking further information from Thailand's Narcotics Suppression Bureau and Royal Thai Police.
He said the operation was conducted on Nov 11 at four locations following intelligence on cross-border drug smuggling.
The operation involved Thai police, the military and the country's Office of the Narcotics Control Board.
"An initial raid in Prachuap Khiri Khan led to the arrest of two Malaysian men and the seizure of 120kg of methamphetamine from a black Toyota Alphard.
"A second raid uncovered another 120kg of methamphetamine in a separate black Toyota Alphard," he said.
The five Malaysian suspects, aged between 34 and 40, comprised four men from Kedah and one from Selangor. Two had previous drug-related records.
All five had entered Thailand through the Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration Complex on different dates. Two Thai women, aged 24 and 25, were also arrested.
The drugs were concealed in modified luxury multi-purpose vehicles with hidden compartments resembling car audio systems.
Thai investigations indicated that the syndicate was allegedly controlled by a mastermind based in Malaysia.
The seized drugs were estimated to be worth RM29 million in the Malaysian market.

Title: US blue wave reshapes Asia's winners and losers
Article:
A RESOUNDING Democratic takeover of Capitol Hill did more than rattle Asian chipmakers. It set off a macro realignment of foreign policy, energy and trade that could create new winners and losers across Asian markets.
The "blue wave" in the United States midterm elections on Nov 3 triggered an anti-artificial intelligence (AI) market shock, sending the tech-heavy Nasdaq to its steepest fall in 19 months.
Investors feared that incoming Democratic leaders would subject AI companies to stricter scrutiny, including over data centre construction and tax breaks.
Asian equities led the regional retreat in the week of the vote. South Korea's KOSPI and Taiwan's TAIEX each tumbled 12 per cent, dragging the broader MSCI Asia ex Japan index down five per cent.
While Asian markets have recovered some ground, investors remain on edge after an October tech selloff driven by valuation concerns and doubts about the payoff from AI investment, fears since amplified by turmoil at Nvidia, a key engine of the AI boom.
The ramifications of the US elections for Asia extend well beyond data centres.
First, there is US policy in the Middle East. Democratic congressional control could pressure the White House to de-escalate the US-Iran war. Indeed, President Donald Trump said the US was unlikely to strike Iran while negotiations continued, a far cry from the more hawkish rhetoric before the elections.
Markets appear to be pricing in this policy shift. Since the midterms, benchmark Brent crude oil has fallen for a second straight week, dropping nearly 19 per cent to below US$96 a barrel.
Cheaper energy could offer relief across Asia.
Historically, around 80 per cent of oil and 90 per cent of gas transiting the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint was destined for ‌Asian markets, meaning this year's Middle East conflict has hit the region particularly hard.
The countries that stand to benefit the most from falling fuel prices include Japan, South Korea and India.
In addition to weighing on inflation and helping boost growth, declining oil prices should also be positive for Asian energy importers' trade balances, which, all else being equal, could help boost their currencies.
But this is where countries may see greater divergence.
North Asian economies have seen their trade surpluses balloon over the past year on the back of massive AI exports. So, if oil prices and AI demand decline together, the latter could offset the former, leaving large tech exporters as net losers.
That shouldn't be the case for their less tech-exposed neighbours.
Currency markets illustrate the divide. Since Nov 3, South Korea's won and the Taiwan dollar have underperformed their major Asian peers, whereas the Indian rupee, heavily exposed to oil prices but not to tech hardware exports, has appreciated sharply.
A widely held view in the US, echoed by leaders on both sides of the aisle, is that elevated prices were a major factor behind the Democratic landslide.
Policy focused on improving affordability could, therefore, become more prominent in both parties' agendas.
Tariffs played a role in cost-of-living concerns, so the election results may reduce the likelihood that Trump ratchets up his aggressive trade policy, even if he could persist via executive authority.
Given bipartisan concerns about China, trade pressure on Beijing may not ease.
But this could benefit other Asian countries that supply consumer goods, such as Vietnam, Bangladesh, Thailand, Indonesia and India.
Another key affordability issue was healthcare. Efforts by Democrats to lower healthcare costs could accelerate demand for generic drugs and outsourced manufacturing.
India could be well positioned here. The country's generic manufacturers, including Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, produce roughly 20 per cent of the world's generic medicines and already supply about 40 per cent of US demand for generics.
However, nothing is certain. Should Trump leverage his executive powers to escalate Middle East conflicts, any projected relief from inflation or high energy costs would immediately vanish.
Furthermore, if strategic competition with China pushes Washington to loosen domestic constraints on AI development, capital could pivot rapidly back to North Asian hardware exporters, relegating markets like India to the sidelines.
For now, navigating Asia requires recognising that Washington's policy shifts reach far beyond the AI supply chain.
Writing for Reuters, the writer is  founder and chief executive officer of Emmer Capital Partners Ltd and the former head of Asia-Pacific Equity Research at BNP Paribas Securities
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Asean must flex its muscle against transnational crime
Article:
AT the tail end of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila yesterday, the bloc made progress on a slew of collaborations on artificial intelligence, the digital economy and maritime security.
However, like in previous years, Asean barely moved the needle on Myanmar's  civil conflict, military crackdowns and persecutions, preferring to uphold "constructive and principled engagement", a position that won't settle the humanitarian crisis in the country.
About 3.6 million people are displaced inside Myanmar while 1.5 million refugees and asylum seekers, Rohingya in particular, have mostly fled to Malaysia.
Since the 1980s, Malaysia has taken in 126,000 Rohingya registered with the United Nations refugee agency, UNHCR,  and thousands more who are undocumented.
With third countries slow or reluctant to share the load, Malaysia has had to tighten security and registration, allow conditional access to temporary work  and pursue repatriation.
Other than the refugee crisis,  transnational crime is rife within Myanmar in the form of cybercrime, fraud, human trafficking, forced labour and illegal gambling.
According to reports, these criminals have netted US$1.4 billion  since 2015.   China has aggressively cracked down on  syndicates operating in the Kokang region, executing 11 of its core figures in January.
However, action against major syndicates has inadvertently created smaller, more mobile criminal groups that conduct  online scams.   This is why Asean must act now, with Malaysia taking the  lead in a joint anti-scam task force linking police, financial intelligence units, immigration authorities and cybersecurity agencies.
This task force should run joint investigations under agreed procedures for arrests and evidence collection and be able to freeze suspicious bank accounts, cryptocurrency assets and other illicit proceeds.
It should support common extradition and prosecution of offenders while providing repatriation, legal aid and psychological support for victims.
Decades of Asean's tenet of consensus and non-interference has regularly excused inaction, but this task force needs  teeth.  Malaysia is in a position to lead because many of its citizens have lost money and their lives to these criminal networks.
Besides, our National Scam Response Centre provides a good working model.    Asean must also rope in China and the United States, on top of global and regional banks and technology platforms, as scam syndicates operate not just within Southeast Asia.
To make  enforcement work, there has to be political will.   Member states must be committed to tracking the evidence, even when it leads to investigations and indictments of "influential" individuals or businesses.
That, more than any summit communiqué, will show whether Asean can actually protect its people.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 170 Johor students graduate from Indonesian traditional dance programme
Article:
JOHOR BARU: About 170 students from five schools in Johor have completed a three-month programme to learn traditional Indonesian dances and graduated at a ceremony today.
Organised by the Indonesian Consulate-General in Johor Baru, the initiative aimed to strengthen cultural ties between Indonesia and its neighbouring countries.
The students showcased dances representing various Indonesian regions during the graduation ceremony.
Indonesian Consul-General Sigit Suryantoro Widiyanto said cultural diplomacy played an important role in strengthening ties between communities beyond formal government and economic relations.
"While diplomatic and economic relations can be built through agreements on paper, bonds between people are nurtured through the language of art and culture.
"The historical, geographical and shared cultural ties between Indonesia and Malaysia, particularly with Johor, must continue to be strengthened through tangible initiatives.
"Cultural preservation cannot be taken for granted. It must be introduced and passed down to the next generation," he said.
He hoped the programme would continue in the coming years and eventually become an annual initiative involving more schools, with support from the Johor government and state education authorities.
The programme, which began in September, involved students from SK (P) Sultan Ibrahim, SK Larkin 2, SK Ngee Heng, SMK Majidi Baru 2 and Austin Heights International School.
They received training from Indonesian dance instructor Ghasanni Ashabul Jannah, better known as Nona JJ, from West Java.
Among the dances performed were Bajidor Kahot from West Java, Mappadendang from South Sulawesi, Tari Piring, Dayak dance and Ondel-Ondel from Jakarta.
The students also performed Malaysian dances, including Zapin Melayu and Gramiyam, highlighting the two-way cultural exchange promoted by the programme.
Johor Unity, Heritage and Culture Committee chairman P. Pannir Selvam, who attended the ceremony, said the initiative went beyond teaching dance by exposing young people to different cultural traditions.
He said exposure to arts and heritage helped nurture mutual understanding, tolerance and respect among communities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dentist fined RM70,000 for employing unregistered worker, allowing dental procedures
Article:
PETALING JAYA: A dentist was fined RM70,000 by the sessions court here today after being found guilty of two charges of employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner and allowing the person to perform dental procedures at her clinic two years ago.
Judge Noor Ruzilawati Mohd Noor imposed a fine of RM30,000 for the first charge and RM40,000 for the second, with six and seven months' imprisonment respectively in default of payment.
Dr Tong Soo Huan, 38, was charged with employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner under the Dental Act 2018 at a dental clinic in Jalan SS21/1 here at 12.50 pm on May 6, 2024.
The charge was brought under Section 68 of the Dental Act 2018, which provides for a maximum fine of RM300,000 or imprisonment for up to six years, or both.
She was also charged with allowing an individual who was not registered under the Act to practise dentistry at her clinic on the same date and time, under Section 69(a) of the same Act, which carries the same maximum penalty.
According to the facts of the case, on May 6, 2024, a team of enforcement officers from the Selangor State Health Department conducted an inspection at Dr Tong's clinic and found a female staff member scanning a patient's teeth using an iTero Element intraoral scanner.
The inspection found that the staff member was not registered with the Malaysian Dental Council (MDC) as a dental practitioner, while Dr Tong, who was a registered dental practitioner, failed to produce the staff member's annual practising certificate when requested by the enforcement officers.
Earlier, Health Ministry (MOH) prosecuting officer Dr Haznita Zainal Abidin urged the court to impose substantial fines for both charges in the interest of public safety and patient protection, noting that the offences were of a strict liability nature and involved the integrity of the dental profession.
"The accused not only failed to ensure that a registered dental practitioner was on duty throughout the clinic's operating hours, but also deliberately instructed and allowed a clinic staff member whose only qualification was the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) to perform dental procedures, namely intraoral scanning using specialised medical device equipment at the accused's premises.
"An oral scanning procedure using an intraoral scanner (iTero Element) requires a high level of expertise to operate. Based on testimony from the Medical Device Authority, the device can only be operated by qualified medical or dental practitioners," she said.
Dr Haznita said the sentence should send a strong message and serve as a stern lesson to the accused and the entire dental practitioner community in Malaysia not to take shortcuts to cut costs or disregard the law by delegating clinical duties to staff without professional qualifications.
However, lawyer Rejinder Singh, representing Dr Tong, appealed for a lighter fine, arguing that his client was a first-time offender and had no previous record of offences under the Dental Act 2018.
"The offence committed was a technical violation and did not involve any criminal element, as a patient had come to the clinic for treatment while Dr Tong was out for lunch at the time.
"The accused is aware of her actions and regrets not exercising greater vigilance in supervising the clinic staff. She has pledged to ensure stricter control measures in the future," the lawyer said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No Cabinet reshuffle needed for now, says Anwar
Article:
MANILA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has dismissed speculation of a Cabinet reshuffle, saying the government remains stable and focused on delivering its policies.
He said there was no pressing need for a reshuffle despite discussions following DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke's resignation as transport minister.
"The government is stable now, policies are discussed comprehensively in the Cabinet, and I work with ministers from various parties.
"We work, share, discuss and have a common position, including on sensitive bilateral, multilateral and Asean issues," he told a media conference on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits here today.
On Loke's resignation, Anwar said he respected the DAP leader's principled stance, although he had earlier asked him to reconsider.
"He, on principle, asked me to accept his resignation, which I have yet to do. But I respect his position because it is important to him to uphold the principles he stands for," he said.
Loke announced his resignation on Nov 10 following the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Anwar dismissed claims of government instability as part of a political campaign, saying the administration would remain focused on delivering for the country.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ismail resigns as Negri Sembilan MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Ismail Lasim has resigned as Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar, with Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi receiving a copy of his resignation letter today.
BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the letter was addressed to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
In a statement, Zambry said BN respected Ismail's decision and thanked him for his service throughout his tenure as Menteri Besar.
He said the party hoped the decision would pave the way for a new chapter in restoring political stability and ensuring the smooth administration of the state.
"BN will extend its full cooperation to ensure an orderly leadership transition, taking into account the position of the majority of state assemblymen and the decree of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar," he said.
Zambry said Zahid would submit a proposed candidate for the new menteri besar to the Ruler soon, in accordance with the provisions of the Negri Sembilan State Constitution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka, Negri Sembilan victories could strengthen PN-BN cooperation, says Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
KOTA BARU: The recent election victories in Negri Sembilan and Melaka could serve as a catalyst for stronger political cooperation between Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN).
Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the outcomes should be leveraged to strengthen mutual understanding, cooperation and public confidence in both coalitions' ability to provide better leadership and governance.
"The victories should be utilised to expand mutual understanding, strengthen consensus and build public confidence in the ability of both coalitions to offer better leadership and administration to the country," he said.
The Kubang Kerian member of parliament said the Melaka election results also highlighted the need for PN component parties, including Wawasan Negara, Gerakan and the Malaysian Indian People's Party (MIPP), to strengthen their election machinery.
He said efforts to increase membership and establish more branches should translate into organisational strength that could be effectively mobilised, particularly during elections.
Every party fielding candidates must have strong election machinery, while other component parties should support them in the spirit of cooperation and shared responsibility, he added.
BN secured a
simple majority
in Saturday's Melaka election, winning 15 of the 28 seats to form the next state government, Election Commission chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sri Lanka gets FBI help to crack down on online scammers
Article:
COLOMBO: The FBI will help Sri Lankan law enforcement detect cyber scammers who have shifted illicit operations to the island following a crackdown in Southeast Asian countries, the US embassy said Monday.
Police say scam networks have increasingly moved operations to Sri Lanka – an attractive destination owing to its relaxed visa regime and reliable, high-speed internet.
"FBI personnel will work with Sri Lankan law enforcement partners on investigative techniques, digital forensics and case development" in a bid to disrupt transnational criminal networks operating out of the South Asian nation, the US embassy in Colombo said in a statement.
An FBI team will spend a week in Sri Lanka this month training local investigators and helping to identify victims, trace criminal activity and build stronger cases against those responsible for online scams, the embassy added.
Fraud compounds, where scammers lure internet users into fake romantic relationships, cryptocurrency investments and betting platforms, have flourished across Southeast Asia.
Initially targeting largely Chinese speakers, the criminal groups behind the compounds have expanded their operations into multiple languages.
Those conducting the scams are sometimes willing con artists, while others are trafficked foreign nationals forced to work.
Officials say the networks operating in Sri Lanka target victims across Asia, including in India, Vietnam and the Philippines, but there are growing concerns that Sri Lankans could be next.
Since the start of the year, Sri Lankan police have arrested more than 1,100 foreigners, mainly from China, Vietnam and India, for alleged involvement in cybercrime.
Sri Lanka has also sought help from China, which pledged closer cooperation on combatting cybercrime.
Beijing's embassy in Colombo said in March that activity in Sri Lanka had risen following enforcement actions in Cambodia, Myanmar and the United Arab Emirates. — AFP

Title: PH MPs challenge Ahmad Maslan to resign over remarks during Budget debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan (PH) MPs have challenged Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan to resign over remarks he made during a Dewan Rakyat debate today.
Port Dickson MP Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said Ahmad's use of the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 committee-stage winding-up session for the Works Ministry to make politically charged remarks was inappropriate for a member of the unity government.
Aminuddin said nearly 29 MPs had raised questions during the debate, but the answers given failed to address the issues.
"We saw that the questions which should have been answered were not properly addressed. Instead, this platform was used to make political and excessively provocative remarks, which is deeply disappointing for a unity government. This should not have happened, especially from a deputy minister representing the minister this afternoon.
"Therefore, I feel that if he does not agree with the government in place today, he should leave the government," he said at a press conference at the Parliament building today.
Sri Gading MP Aminolhuda Hassan said the Pontian MP's remarks were inappropriate for a deputy minister in the Madani government, who should have taken a more measured approach.
"As an MP from Johor, and he (Ahmad) is also an MP from Johor, I feel that Johoreans are generally more measured in their language. But if he feels that he disagrees with the approach being taken today, then he can leave his position," he said.
Meanwhile, Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong said Ahmad must uphold collective responsibility and defend the administration rather than make sarcastic remarks during the winding-up session.
"If a deputy minister makes such remarks while winding up the debate and takes jibes at the existing government, he should resign. If he says things like that, he is being unprofessional and is no longer fit to serve as a deputy minister," he said, adding that Ahmad should resign if he refused to retract his remarks.
Hulu Langat MP Mohd Sany Hamzan also challenged Ahmad to step down immediately if he was no longer aligned with the unity government.
"I just want to challenge Ahmad Maslan. If he is no longer comfortable with the Madani government and the unity government in place today, I challenge him to resign. Resign immediately. Do not become arrogant, conceited, boastful or egoistic over the victory you secured in Melaka," he said.
Ahmad drew criticism earlier during the winding-up session after reciting a pantun touching on political support for Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN).
He delivered the pantun in response to an interjection by Datuk Rosol Wahid (PN-Hulu Terengganu), who questioned whether the promise to abolish tolls had been made solely to win elections.
Earlier, Datuk Ngeh Koo Ham (PH-Beruas) had asked whether the government could reduce tolls in stages, citing the 30 per cent reduction in highway toll rates after 2018 as an example.

Title: Malaysia calls for stronger Asean-South Korea cooperation against online scams
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has called for stronger cooperation between Asean and South Korea to combat cross-border crime, particularly online scams.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the issue was among the key matters raised by Malaysia at the 27th Asean-Republic of Korea (Asean-ROK) Summit, alongside efforts to expand trade, investment and cooperation in artificial intelligence (AI) and the digital economy.
He said the summit also discussed the future direction of dialogue relations and strategic cooperation between Asean and South Korea.
"Malaysia also supports an approach of continuous dialogue and peaceful resolution to ensure peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula.
"This commitment reflects Malaysia's stance to continue strengthening regional cooperation and international relations for mutual benefit," he said in a post on X.
South Korea is Asean's fifth-largest trading partner, with trade valued at RM851.76 billion in 2024.
South Korean foreign direct investment into the Asean region amounted to RM30.71 billion in the same year.
Anwar is leading the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits in Manila from Nov 15 to 17.

Title: Man jailed for life over Dublin knife attack that sparked riots
Article:
DUBLIN: An Algerian-Irish man was jailed for life Monday for attempted murder following a 2023 Dublin knife attack that injured multiple children and sparked rioting and looting.
Riad Bouchaker, 52, was found guilty in July of eight charges arising from the attack outside a school in central Dublin on Nov 23, 2023, which left a 5-year-old girl and a woman in her 30s in a critical condition.
The young girl, who was stabbed in the heart by Bouchaker, suffered a catastrophic brain injury and is now non-verbal, uses a wheelchair and is fed by a tube in her stomach as she cannot swallow safely.
A 5-year-old boy and a 6-year-old girl were also injured.
Childcare worker Leanne Flynn, who intervened to protect the children, suffered serious injuries and underwent emergency surgery.
Within hours of the attack, misinformation about the suspect's identity spread online, fuelling anger among anti-immigration activists and far-right groups.
The worst rioting seen in the Irish capital for decades erupted in the city centre as crowds clashed with police, set vehicles on fire and looted shops.
The violence shocked the country and triggered days of debate over immigration, online misinformation and public order.
Almost 100 people were arrested, with more than 80 charged with offences.
During his trial, Bouchaker pleaded not guilty to three counts of attempted murder and three counts of assault causing harm.
He also denied one count each of intentionally or recklessly causing serious harm, and brandishing a dangerous weapon – a 36cm-long (14-inch) kitchen knife.
Judge Tony Hunt told the jury that two years before the attack, Bouchaker had suffered from a benign brain tumour that required surgery.
Hunt also said that due to interventions by bystanders immediately after the attack, Bouchaker suffered a head injury that required hospital treatment.
He was found fit to stand trial, and "there is no suggestion that he was suffering mental disorder at the time of the incident", the judge said.
Evidence was heard from more than 80 witnesses, including eyewitnesses, emergency responders, police and forensic experts.

Title: Grab drivers in trial pay lower commissions, record higher earnings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Grab drivers participating in a government-backed trial are paying lower commissions and recording higher earnings, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said 170,944 driver-partners had joined the Grab Service Fee proof of concept as at May 31, 2026.
The trial recorded an average service fee of 18 per cent and an effective rate of 15 per cent, below the current 20 per cent commission cap.
It also saw earnings per minute in transit increase by more than 66 per cent compared with before drivers joined the trial.
Hasbi was replying to Bagan Serai member of parliament Datuk Idris Ahmad during the committee-stage debate on the Transport Ministry's Budget 2027 allocation.
He said the trial followed a proposal by Grab Car Sdn Bhd for a more flexible fare structure, with dynamic commission rates subject to a weekly or monthly average cap of 20 per cent.
The structure takes into account distance, location and trip duration, as well as drivers' movement between drop-off and pick-up points.
"This is still in the proof of concept stage," he said.
Hasbi said the Transport Ministry, through the Land Public Transport Agency, had capped e-hailing commissions at 20 per cent for private vehicles and 10 per cent for taxis, hire cars, airport taxis and luxury taxis.
He said the government acknowledged drivers' concerns over commission rates and would continue studying the issue to safeguard their welfare and interests.
Earlier this month, the government said it would
review the 20 per cent cap
following concerns that the rate was eating into drivers' earnings.
On safety, Hasbi said licensed e-hailing platforms were required to include an emergency function connecting directly to the 999 emergency line. It must also alert the platform's emergency system and a contact nominated by the driver or passenger.
He was responding to Putatan MP Datuk Shahelmey Yahya, who called for accident alerts to be made compulsory in delivery and e-hailing apps following the death of a p-hailing rider in the Klang Valley in late October.

Title: Zetrix offers RM100mil upfront, 6-month instalments to settle RTD arrears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has offered to pay RM100 million upfront to be reappointed as a Road Transport Department (RTD) revenue collection agent, with the remaining RM214 million in arrears to be settled over six months.
Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah told the Dewan Rakyat today that the proposal had been referred to the Finance Ministry, while a RM29 million penalty had been imposed on the company under the terms of its agreement.
He said Zetrix AI, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, submitted the proposal in a letter to the Transport Ministry dated Nov 5.
The remaining RM214 million would be paid in 6 equal monthly instalments of RM35.67 million. The ministry forwarded the proposal to the Finance Ministry on Nov 10.
"The total penalty imposed is RM29 million based on the terms and conditions of the agreement," he said.
My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd, both under the MYEG Group,
failed to remit
RM314 million in government revenue collected between May 19 and Sept 30.
The RTD
suspended both companies
as its collection agents effective Oct 5.
Explaining why the company had been given more time, Hasbi said it had repeatedly committed to settling the outstanding revenue after receiving reminder letters.
He said extensions were granted because the company was still providing services and the government wanted to avoid disruptions.
These included online payment of summonses by foreigners at Malaysia-Singapore border entry points and computerised theory test centres in Sabah and Sarawak, as e-testing was only expected to be fully available by 2028.
Hasbi said MyEG handled 61.16 per cent of collections through collection agents and 13.27 per cent of the department's total revenue as at Sept 30.
He added that the ministry's legal adviser had taken steps to issue a notice of demand, with court action to follow if payment was not made within the stipulated period, after consultation with the Attorney-General's Chambers.
However, he said the notice and court action would not proceed if the government accepted Zetrix AI's settlement proposal.
An MP later questioned the proposal to reappoint the company as a collection agent as part of the arrangement to recover its outstanding payments.
Hasbi replied that the proposal was now with the Finance Ministry for consideration.
On Oct 27, then transport minister Anthony Loke said
full settlement
of all outstanding payments, including late-transfer penalties, was a precondition for any extension or further operational consideration.

Title: Anwar welcomes Indonesia's commitment to tackling transboundary haze
Article:
MANILA: Malaysia and other Asean member states have welcomed Indonesia's commitment to addressing the issue of transboundary haze.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the issue was raised by Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto himself during the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits today.
Acknowledging the complexity of the issue, Anwar said he was optimistic that Indonesia's approach would yield positive results.
"President Prabowo took the initiative to raise the issue of haze and its impact on neighbouring countries. We said we were ready to cooperate, and he outlined the measures being taken.
"We acknowledge that the issue is complex and difficult to resolve, but we are pleased with Indonesia's commitment and cooperation with Asean countries to, if not prevent it entirely, at least reduce its impact in the future," said Anwar at a press conference here.
Anwar said Malaysia and other neighbouring countries, including Singapore, were also encouraged by the development and had pledged to continue assisting Indonesia in addressing the issue.
Earlier during the plenary session,
Prabowo apologised
to Malaysia and Singapore, which have been affected by transboundary haze caused by forest fires in Indonesia.
He also assured that various efforts were being undertaken to tackle the forest and land fires.
The fires in Indonesia have reportedly been burning for nearly four months, causing transboundary haze that has affected communities in Malaysia and Singapore.

Title: Malaysia's ITU Council seat opens door to early 6G discussions, says Fahmi
Article:
DOHA: Malaysia's successful bid to retain its seat on the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Council for the 2027-2030 term will give the country greater opportunities to participate in early discussions on sixth-generation (6G) communications technology and the future of global connectivity.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Malaysia's continued membership of the ITU's highest decision-making body would enable the country to play an active role in setting telecommunications standards, managing spectrum and shaping international connectivity policies.
He said Malaysia's participation was also important in sharing its experience in developing 5G networks while amplifying the voices of developing countries in global decision-making.
"I believe Malaysia's presence at this highest level, under the auspices of the United Nations, creates opportunities for us not only to share our experience in rolling out 5G and beyond.
"In fact, we now have early access to discussions on next-generation connectivity, or what is known as 6G," he said, commenting on Malaysia's next steps following its re-election to the ITU Council.
Fahmi said Malaysia's experience in developing telecommunications technology could serve as a benchmark for other countries, particularly in identifying challenges and mitigating risks at the early stages of implementation.
"This is important because our experience can serve as a lesson on what to avoid and what needs to be examined early on, while allowing developing countries to have a voice and take part in decision-making," he said.
Fahmi also thanked the teams at the Communications Ministry, the Foreign Ministry (Wisma Putra) and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for their commitment to securing Malaysia's continued membership of the international body.
"I would like to congratulate everyone at the Communications Ministry, Wisma Putra and MCMC on this remarkable achievement," he said.
Malaysia retained its seat on the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term following an election held during the 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) in Doha.

Title: Ringgit ends mostly higher against major currencies, slips against greenback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended mostly higher against major currencies and Asean peers on Monday but weakened against the greenback as the US interest rate outlook remained hawkish.
At 6pm, the local currency eased to 4.0915/0960 versus the greenback from Friday's close of 4.0845/0890.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar remained well-supported with the US Dollar Index hovering at 103.398 points ahead of the Fed's Federal Open Market Committee meeting in December.
"The futures market has shown that the odds of a 25-basis-point rate hike have risen to more than 100 per cent. The question now is whether a 50-basis-point hike could happen at the upcoming meeting. Hence, this has led to greater demand for the US dollar," he told Bernama.
The ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
It strengthened against the euro to 4.5039/5089 from 4.5166/5216 at last Friday's close, appreciated vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.3955/4014 from 5.4046/4106, but edged down against the Japanese yen to 2.5638/5666 from 2.5549/5579.
The ringgit also traded mostly higher against its Asean peers.
It rose vis-à-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 223.9/224.3 from 224.3/224.6, went up against the Philippine peso to 6.40/6.41 from 6.41/6.42, and climbed against the Thai baht to 12.0576/0755 from 12.0611/0833.
However, the local note inched down against the Singapore dollar to 3.1737/1772 from 3.1729/1769.

Title: [UPDATED] Bukit Aman verifying nationality of suspect killed in Philippines drug bust
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman is verifying the nationality of a man believed to be Malaysian who was killed during a drug bust involving RM858,000 worth of methamphetamine in Tawi-Tawi, southern Philippines, yesterday.
Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the initial belief that the suspect was Malaysian was based on a private clinic card issued in Sabah that was found on him.
He said Philippine authorities had shared details of the incident with Malaysian police.
However, the man's nationality had yet to be confirmed as no official identification documents were found on him.
"We have been provided with details of the case by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA).
"We are working on identifying him," he said when contacted today.
The suspect, identified by Philippine authorities as Janimal Hajad, also known as "Ungod", was killed alongside his alleged Filipino accomplice, Sansibar Amirul Amil, during a buy-bust operation in Barangay Tubig Mampallam, Bongao, Tawi-Tawi.
According to the Philippine News Agency (PNA), the operation took place at 4.50pm yesterday and involved PDEA agents supported by Philippine police and marines.
PDEA Tawi-Tawi provincial officer Abraham Solon Kalim said the 2 suspects allegedly opened fire on enforcement personnel after realising they were dealing with undercover anti-narcotics agents.
The suspects reportedly attempted to escape aboard a motorised wooden boat while firing at the enforcement team.
Both men were killed in the ensuing exchange of gunfire.
Two unidentified women were also wounded by stray bullets and taken to hospital for treatment.
No casualties were reported among enforcement personnel.
Authorities seized about 2kg of suspected methamphetamine, valued at 13.4 million pesos (RM858,000), packed in two Chinese tea bags.
A pistol and the motorised wooden boat allegedly intended for the suspects' escape were also recovered.
Philippine authorities are continuing their investigation into the incident.

Title: Pos Malaysia Q3 net loss widens despite revenue growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pos Malaysia Bhd's net loss widened to RM62.25 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM45.23 million a year earlier, mainly due to one-off charges related to vessel impairments and the closure of Pos Shop.
Revenue for the quarter rose 8.3 per cent to RM501.22 million from RM462.77 million, supported by growth across all business segments.
The increase was driven by higher parcel volumes in its courier business, alongside stronger contributions from Pos Aviation, Pos Logistics and other businesses, including digital certification, data services and Pos Ar-Rahnu.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, Pos Malaysia narrowed its net loss to RM125.26 million from RM132.17 million a year earlier, while revenue rose to RM1.48 billion from RM1.37 billion.
The postal segment's nine-month revenue increased 2.5 per cent to RM808.2 million, as higher parcel volumes partially offset the continued structural decline in mail volumes and retail footfall.
Its pre-tax loss narrowed to RM115.4 million from RM116.2 million.
The aviation segment recorded a 15.2 per cent increase in revenue to RM323.7 million, driven by higher cargo volumes, increased flight movements and growth in inflight catering.
Pos Logistics sustained its turnaround, with nine-month revenue rising 23.4 per cent to RM202.3 million on stronger performance in its automotive, freight, shipping and warehousing businesses.
The segment's pre-tax loss narrowed to RM29.6 million from RM31.9 million, despite a RM15 million impairment charge on vessels.
Group chief executive officer Charles Brewer said the third-quarter results reflected ongoing efforts to reshape Pos Malaysia.
"Every business segment is growing, led by our courier business, and our nine-month loss before tax is narrowing. We are strengthening the basics of the business, giving us a firmer foundation to build on.
"With the year-end peak ahead, we are ready to build on this momentum. Our focus is clear: keep improving efficiency through disciplined operational focus and, of course, further leveraging digital innovation and artificial intelligence (AI)," he said in a statement.
Pos Malaysia said the domestic parcel delivery market remained highly competitive and faced structural challenges.
The company expects parcel volumes to increase during the year-end peak season, building on market share gains achieved so far.
It will continue to focus on business transformation, digital and AI-driven efficiency, disciplined cost management and regulatory reform.
"The board expects financial performance for financial year 2026 to remain challenging, with the pace of recovery dependent on, among others, the implementation of a sustainable universal service obligation funding framework," it said.

Title: Johor dengue cases surge 159pct, deaths rise to 18
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor recorded 13,641 dengue cases and 18 deaths as of yesterday, marking a 159.4 per cent increase in infections and an 80 per cent rise in fatalities compared with the corresponding period last year.
State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said 275 cases were reported in Epidemiological Week 45, up 3.4 per cent from 266 cases the previous week.
Johor Baru recorded the highest number of cases last week, with 173 or 62.9 per cent of the state total, followed by Kulai with 70 cases (25.5 per cent).
The remaining cases were reported in Kluang and Pontian (seven each), Segamat (six), Kota Tinggi (four), Muar (three), Mersing and Batu Pahat (two each), and Tangkak (one).
Ling said 17 new dengue outbreak localities were reported during the week, comprising 10 in Johor Baru, six in Kulai and one in Kluang.
The cumulative number of outbreak localities reached 1,489 this year, compared with 532 during the corresponding period last year, an increase of 180 per cent.
He said enforcement operations had resulted in 5,338 compounds worth RM2.669 million being issued this year, of which 76.19 per cent had been paid.
However, inspections continued to uncover potential mosquito breeding sites inside and outside homes, indicating that residents were still not doing enough to eliminate stagnant water.
Ling called on the public to spend at least 10 minutes checking and eliminating potential Aedes breeding grounds at home and workplaces, including containers that could collect stagnant water.
Residents were also advised to cover water storage containers, remove stagnant water and scrub containers to eliminate mosquito larvae.
Schools were encouraged to organise regular clean-up activities, while school bus operators and drivers were advised to use aerosol sprays inside buses before morning and afternoon student journeys.
